terms.grammar: adjective and pronoun; “different from” is alius ac (atque)
evidence: Ter. Ph. 684: aliud mihi respondēs ac rogō?
Sall. Cat. 6.2: alius aliō mōre vīventēs
Ter. And. 189: nunc hic diēs aliam vītam affert, aliōs mōrēs postulat
terms.comment: Latin says “different” with alius: alius ac (atque) is “different from”; aliud est … aliud … is “… is one thing, … another”; and a doubled alius gives “each a different …”: alius aliō mōre, each in a different way.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 3.7.5: tū sī aliter exīstimās, “if you think differently”
Tac. Ann. 6.28: ā cēterīs avibus dīversum
terms.comment: Stronger than alius: turned the other way, contrary.

terms.grammar: adjective, with a genitive or dative
verb, irregular; intransitive in this sense, with ab
evidence: Cic. Caecin. 39: quid hoc ab illō differt?
terms.comment: Transitive, the same verb means “put off”, “postpone”.

phrases.latin: Eho, verberō, aliud mihi respondēs ac rogō?
phrases.english: Hey, you rascal, you’re answering something different from what I asked?
hurrying is one thing, rushing another

phrases.latin: disparī genere, dissimilī linguā, alius aliō mōre vīventēs
phrases.english: of different stock and different speech, each living in a different way

phrases.latin: nōn vidēs quam dīversus sit dēscendentium habitus et ēscendentium?
phrases.english: don’t you see how differently people carry themselves going down and going up?
